2. 
3. In-scope (verification-order) targets — the **only** functions this View must
4. serve, and the only ones any later phase may annotate:
5. 
6. - `PageDirectoryEntryFlags::new`
7. - `PageDirectoryEntry::new`
8. - `PageDirectoryEntry::is_present`
9. - `PageDirectoryEntryFlags::is_present`
10. - `PageDirectoryEntry::frame_address`
11. 
12. All other items (`is_user`, `is_writable`, `is_large_page`, the `set_*`
13. mutators, `from_raw_value`/`into_raw_value`, `flags`, `frame_number`, the `SIZE`
14. const, the `TableEntry` impl, derived `Debug`/`Clone`/`Copy`) are **out of
15. scope** and untouched. Where they are mentioned below it is only to confirm the
16. View would *also* serve them without redesign.
17. 
18. ---
19. 
20. ## Abstract Resource
21. 
22. This module models **one x86 32-bit page-directory entry**: a value that binds
23. a set of **paging control flags** to a **physical frame** (the page table — or,
24. for a large page, the mapped region — that the entry points at). To a caller a
25. PDE is conceptually the pair
26. 
27. ```
28. ( flags , frame )
29. ```
30. 
31. an installable / decodable slot in a page directory. From it callers read back
32. exactly two abstract facts in scope: **is it present?** and **what physical base
33. address does it point at?** (`frame << FRAME_SHIFT`).
34. 
35. Two types need abstraction, mirroring the source structure:
36. 
37. | Type | What it is to a caller |
38. |------|------------------------|
39. | `PageDirectoryEntryFlags` | an immutable bundle of the eight paging control bits |
40. | `PageDirectoryEntry`      | the pair `(flags, frame)` |
41. 
42. It is *not* a collection, allocator, or state machine: both types are
43. immutable, `Copy`, pure-value tokens. Every in-scope function is either a pure
44. total constructor (`*::new`) or a pure read-only query (`is_present`,
45. `frame_address`); none mutate, allocate, fail, or panic.
46. 
47. ### Downstream contract this View must realize
48. 
49. The verified kernel already pins the *external* contract of these types in
50. `src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.spec.rs`:
51. 
52. - the types are lifted opaque via `external_type_specification`
53.   (`ExPageDirectoryEntry`, `ExPageDirectoryEntryFlags`);
54. - four **placeholder** `assume_specification`s (currently signature-only, no
55.   `ensures`) stand in for `PageDirectoryEntryFlags::new`,
56.   `PageDirectoryEntry::new`, `PageDirectoryEntry::is_present`,
57.   `PageDirectoryEntry::frame_address`.
58. 
59. The View below is chosen so that, once `arch` is verified, the real `ensures`
60. (the spec transitions in this document) **supersede** those placeholders without
61. breaking kernel proofs. The frame index reuses the already-shipped
62. `FrameNumber` abstraction (`frame@ : int`, bounded by `FrameNumber::spec_max()`)
63. and the frame/page size reuses the existing `mem::FRAME_SIZE` spec constant —
64. the same one `FrameNumber::spec_max()` is defined over — so the address
65. `frame@ * FRAME_SIZE` is the inverse of the `frame` passed to `new`.
66. 
67. ---
68. 
69. ## View Types
70. 
71. ### `PageDirectoryEntryFlags`
72. 
73. The abstract value of a flags bundle is exactly its **eight boolean control
74. bits**. Each source enum is two-valued (`0` = clear, `1 << SHIFT` = set), i.e.
75. isomorphic to `bool`; the spec-world form of "the bit is set" is a `bool`.
76. 
77. ```rust
78. pub struct PdeFlagsView {
79.     /// Present (P) bit — the entry maps something.
80.     pub present: bool,
81.     /// Read/Write (R/W) bit — writes permitted (`is_writable`).
82.     pub writable: bool,
83.     /// User/Supervisor (U/S) bit — user-mode access permitted (`is_user`).
84.     pub user: bool,
85.     /// Page-Write-Through (PWT) bit.
86.     pub write_through: bool,
87.     /// Page-Cache-Disable (PCD) bit.
88.     pub cache_disabled: bool,
89.     /// Accessed (A) bit.
90.     pub accessed: bool,
91.     /// Dirty (D) bit.
92.     pub dirty: bool,
93.     /// Page-Size (PS) bit — entry maps a large page (`is_large_page`).
94.     pub large_page: bool,
95. }
96. 
97. impl View for PageDirectoryEntryFlags {
98.     type V = PdeFlagsView;
99.     // `closed`: callers reference `self@.present` etc., but the bit-packing into
100.     // the raw `PteWord` is hidden — exactly the encoding-independence the caller
101.     // analysis demands.
102.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> PdeFlagsView;
103. }
104. ```
105. 
106. ### `PageDirectoryEntry`
107. 
108. A PDE is the pair `(flags, frame)`. The frame is abstracted as its integer
109. index (the `FrameNumber` View, `int`); the physical base address it yields is
110. *derived* (`frame * FRAME_SIZE`), never stored.
111. 
112. ```rust
113. pub struct PdeView {
114.     /// The eight control bits this entry was built with.
115.     pub flags: PdeFlagsView,
116.     /// The frame index this entry points at (== the inner `FrameNumber`'s `@`).
117.     pub frame: int,
118. }
119. 
120. impl View for PageDirectoryEntry {
121.     type V = PdeView;
122.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> PdeView;
123. }
124. ```
125. 
126. ---
127. 
128. ## Well-formedness Invariants
129. 
130. ```rust
131. impl PageDirectoryEntryFlags {
132.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
133.         true   // every combination of the eight bits is a legal flags value
134.     }
135. }
136. ```
137. 
138. A flags bundle has no cross-field constraint: all 2⁸ combinations are
139. constructible by `new`, so its invariant is vacuous. (Kept explicit for
140. uniformity; it adds no obligation.)
141. 
142. ```rust
143. impl PageDirectoryEntry {
144.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
145.         // The frame index is a valid frame number, so the derived physical base
146.         // address `frame * FRAME_SIZE` is well-defined and cannot overflow
147.         // `usize`. This is exactly the bound `FrameNumber` already guarantees;
148.         // restating it here lets `frame_address` be total with no `requires`.
149.         &&& 0 <= self.frame <= FrameNumber::spec_max()
150.         &&& self.flags.inv()
151.     }
152. }
153. ```
154. 
155. The only real constraint is the frame bound, inherited verbatim from the
156. `FrameNumber` type invariant. It is what makes `frame_address` total and
157. overflow-free — the single guarantee the caller analysis pins on it.
158.

 This module models **one x86 32-bit page-directory entry**: a value that binds

 ```
